clue.text: Hip proportions said to be cut

indicators.note: said signals that the words are heard spoken, not read as spelt

parts.note: hip means fashionable, IN, and proportions are SIZES; spoken together they give the entry

explanation.surface: A remark about measuring someone's hips, with a hint that they have been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Hip here is the slang for trendy, IN, not the body part; IN SIZES spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make an incision is to cut into something with a blade.

clue.text: Effect of Independent politician over Bill

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed on top, so the first pieces come before the law

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
a bill once passed becomes an act

explanation.surface: The effect of a lone independent politician voting on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an impact is a strong effect or influence.

clue.text: Thoughtful purchasing sweetheart's clothing

indicators.note: purchasing means getting hold of, so the thoughtful word takes the sweetheart inside

parts.note: thoughtful means caring
pet is a term of endearment, a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A kind partner buying their sweetheart some clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchasing means acquiring, so it holds the pet inside; the 's is has, a link. Clothing is fair: carpet dresses a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor: carpet covers a floor as garments cover a body.

clue.text: Join admitting one's mercenary?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the join takes the one inside

parts.note: to solder is to join metal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone signing up for pay makes them a hired gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a mercenary is one kind of fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mercenary is a hired fighting man, one type of serving warrior.

clue.text: Ancient port used by sailors

parts.note: not a harbour town but the left side of a ship, in the old term sailors once used for it

explanation.surface: An old harbour town once frequented by seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: Port reads as a harbour, but it is the left-hand side of a ship; the old nautical word for that side is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic nautical term for the left side of a vessel, later replaced to avoid confusion with starboard.

clue.text: Previously good and eager

parts.note: ago means previously, in the past

explanation.surface: Someone who was once good and keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: agog means excitedly keen to hear or see something.

clue.text: They make bread taking money, essentially

definitions.text: They make bread taking money, essentially

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the bread makers hold the extra letter

parts.note: bakers make bread

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word money

explanation.surface: Financiers earn their dough by taking other people's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' puts N, the middle of money, inside BAKERS. The whole clue also defines: bread is slang for money, which financiers make by taking deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: bread is slang for cash, and financiers earn it from the funds they hold.

clue.text: Blokes absorbed by plug change

indicators.note: absorbed by means soaked up inside, so the men go within the plug

parts.note: a plug is an advert, AD
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Some lads swapping a plug for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: Plug is the advertising sense, a promotional mention, not the electrical fitting. Blokes is British slang for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to amend a text is to change or correct it.

clue.text: 'Bad' is as 'terrible' to describe tragedy

indicators.note: to describe here means to draw round, so the quoted words enclose the answer

explanation.surface: A language note: calling a tragedy bad is as weak as calling it terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: Describe has its geometric sense, to trace around, so the words 'Bad' is as 'terrible' wrap round the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a calamity or catastrophe is a terrible misfortune.

clue.text: Colour is flawless round pearl's exterior

indicators.note: round says the word for flawless goes around the other piece

parts.note: flawless means pure

indicators.note: the exterior of the word pearl is its outside letters only

explanation.surface: Praise of a gem: its colour is perfect around the pearl's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of pearl's belongs with 'exterior': the pearl's exterior is its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a shade between red and blue, the colour of royalty.

clue.text: Versatile players, all missing game

indicators.note: missing tells us the word all is dropped from the longer phrase

parts.note: versatile players in cricket, good at both batting and bowling, are all-rounders

explanation.surface: A team of versatile players all failing to show up for the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' takes ALL away from ALL-ROUNDERS. Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, like a simple baseball, played mostly in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a traditional British bat-and-ball team sport.

clue.text: Cheddar's rind, palatable and easy to swallow

indicators.note: a cheese's rind is its outside, so take the first and last letters of Cheddar

parts.note: palatable means fit to eat, edible

explanation.surface: A cheese note: even the rind of this Cheddar is tasty and goes down easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rind' gives CR, the outside letters of Cheddar. 'Easy to swallow' is figurative: easy to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a story that is easy to swallow is believable.

clue.text: Record from holding stick, running

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the record contains the stick

parts.note: a log is a record
to pin is to stick, as to a board

explanation.surface: Someone holding a stick from a record while running.
explanation.walkthrough: From is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a loping animal runs with a long, easy, bounding stride.

clue.text: Stones lacking heart give heartless lyrics

indicators.note: heartless means the word give loses its middle letters, keeping its two ends

parts.note: odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint about stones and cold, unfeeling song lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' leaves GE from give. 'Stones lacking heart' is a fair definition: these rocks are hollow inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: hollow rocks with crystal-lined cavities inside, so stones whose centres are empty.

clue.text: Purist, extremely discriminating and not tolerant initially

definitions.text: Purist, extremely discriminating and not tolerant initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A description of a fussy purist who is choosy and intolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purist' looks like the definition, and is part of it, but the whole clue defines while 'initially' takes the first letters of all six words.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a stickler fussily insistent on rules and petty detail.

clue.text: Bubbly Perrier? Bliss with European bubbly

indicators.note: bubbly describes letters fizzing about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sparkling-water advert: Perrier is bliss, and European fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second the signal to rearrange the brand and bliss into IRREPRESSIBL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bubbly person is lively and cannot be held down.

clue.text: Unusually fat baker's producing croissants?

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters take an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rotund baker making the morning pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a definition by example: croissants are a typical morning meal in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: croissants are a continental first meal of the day.

clue.text: Tree top lifted after log man chopped up

indicators.note: after puts the raised piece behind the shuffled letters
chopped up suggests the words being cut into bits and reassembled
lifted in a down clue means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means top or first-rate

explanation.surface: A man chopping a log into pieces, then lifting off the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped up' turns LOG MAN into MAGNOL; 'lifted' turns AI, crossword A1 meaning top quality, into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flowering shrub or tree with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Gave in with a mutter turning stroppy

indicators.note: turning says these letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who gave in, with a grumble, getting bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stroppy person is quarrelsome and inclined to dispute.

clue.text: One in charge seeing America in trough

indicators.note: in means placed within the feeding trough

parts.note: a manger is a trough for animal feed

explanation.surface: A boss seeing America as a pig in a trough.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who runs a business or team and directs others.

clue.text: Repeat line ignored by educated person

indicators.note: ignored by means left out by, so the line is dropped from the educated person

parts.note: a literate, as a noun, is a person able to read and write

explanation.surface: An educated person who ignores lines on the page, so reads repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to say or do again, as a program loops a step.

clue.text: Tormentor, a Tory, restrains Speaker

indicators.note: restrains means holds in, so the run of words contains the answer

explanation.surface: A political tormentor restraining the Speaker of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the Commons chair, but it is just a public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a public speaker, especially an eloquent one.

clue.text: Refusal to face evil head of Government snooping

indicators.note: to face means to stand in front of, so the refusal comes before the evil

parts.note: no is a refusal
a sin is an evil act

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A government saying no to spying on people, which it regards as evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: nosing about means poking into others' business, like a nosy parker.

clue.text: Follow on, say, caught by appeal

indicators.note: caught by means trapped inside, so the example goes within the appeal

parts.note: to sue is to appeal or petition
say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: following on after being caught by an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: follow on is a rule forcing a side to bat again, caught a dismissal, appeal a shout to the umpire. Here it means move smoothly on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to segue is to pass smoothly from one thing to the next.

clue.text: One barely running on pitch?

parts.note: barely means without clothes, so someone running naked across a sports field

explanation.surface: A sluggish footballer barely managing to run on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Barely reads as hardly, but it means bare: in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a person who dashes naked across a sports ground during a match.

clue.text: Daybreak and desperate man embraces wife

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the man surrounds the wife

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman from the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: At first light a frantic man hugs his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a famous British comic-strip cowboy, a giant who eats cow pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: first light of the morning, sunrise.

clue.text: Sign record or mag unexpectedly

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the two short words come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Signing a record deal, or a magazine one, out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' turns OR MAG into OGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a written symbol standing for a whole word, like the ampersand.

clue.text: Duty to check lavatory's unoccupied

indicators.note: to check is to hold in, so the tax surrounds the toilet

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a duty
can is American slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: An official checking whether the public toilet is free.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, Britain's sales tax. 'Lavatory's' is lavatory is, so the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vacant seat or room is free, with nobody in it.

clue.text: Straying US president against Republican bluster

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president
to rant is to bluster

explanation.surface: A wandering American president sounding off against the Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something aberrant departs from the normal course, wandering off.

clue.text: One detests consuming energy for fire

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the hating one takes in the energy

parts.note: one who detests is a hater
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes wasting energy on a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Fire here is the British sense: an electric or gas fire, a room heating appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in Britain a fire can mean an appliance warming a room.
